recap:
## Decisions
- Drop solar cells; power with rechargeable batteries charged by the base station. [00:21:58]
- No hand dynamo or kinetic charging; battery only. [00:22:17]
- Use a regular chip, not the advanced chip, for cost reasons. [00:22:55]
- Use a simple beep instead of the sample speaker. [00:21:22]
- The case colour is a special yellow. [00:24:47]
- Use plastic instead of rubber to keep within budget; the product is now under the €12.50 cost target. [00:27:29]
- Don't sum the evaluation scores; go ahead based on the general feeling. [00:20:42]

## Action items
- owner not assigned: Find out more about the target market, for example a street evaluation with young people, including whether young children are a market. [00:30:18]
- owner not assigned: Ask the production department to build a real prototype to evaluate at home. [00:32:03]

## Unresolved
- ME was not convinced by the multifunctional buttons and asked about users who want digit buttons. [00:09:17]
- A child might try to eat the banana. [00:06:27]
- There is no cost line for the radio frequency part or the base station. [00:26:39]
- It's unclear whether an integrated circuit is needed for two push buttons and two scroll wheels. [00:31:04]
- It's unclear whether the target price applies to all of Europe or only richer countries. [00:15:55]
- Purchase appeal is in doubt: UI scored it low, and ME said nobody would buy it. [00:27:42]
- Version two could control more than the TV, such as mood lighting and the whole room. [00:31:30]
